name: The Willard InterContinental
insider_take: Where presidents have plotted, deals have been struck, and American history continues to unfold in opulent splendor.
whats_special: This legendary "Crown Jewel of Pennsylvania Avenue" has hosted every U.S. president since Franklin Pierce in 1853. The term "lobbying" was actually coined here in the 1870s when President Ulysses S. Grant would meet with political petitioners in The Willard's grand lobby. Martin Luther King Jr. put the finishing touches on his "I Have a Dream" speech in room 2111, and Abraham Lincoln lived here for 10 days before his inauguration.
pro_tip: Request a Pennsylvania Avenue-facing room for stunning views of the White House and Capitol, or book the Lincoln Suite where the 16th president once resided—it's still decorated with period antiques.
dont_miss: Afternoon tea in Peacock Alley, the hotel's stunning promenade lined with elegant shops, and the famous Round Robin Bar—one of America's oldest continuously operating hotel bars where the mint julep was perfected and political deals are still brokered over cocktails.
pros: Historic luxury hotel with presidential legacy and timeless elegance
Prime location two blocks from White House and National Mall
Exceptional fine dining at Café du Parc and Round Robin Bar
Luxurious spa services and comprehensive fitness facilities
cons: Premium pricing reflects historic luxury positioning
Busy downtown location with urban noise levels
